html:
Smallpox was an infectious disease caused by the variola virus, passed from person to person. It killed about three in ten of those it struck and scarred many survivors. It is the only human disease ever wiped out.

It was old in Asia, Africa and Europe, where most people caught it as children. The peoples of the Americas and Australia had never met it, so when Europeans brought it the deaths were enormous, a large part of the Columbian Exchange.

  • In 1520 it swept Tenochtitlan between the two Spanish assaults (smallpox strikes the Aztecs).
  • It ran ahead of the Spanish into the Andes and probably killed the Inca ruler Huayna Capac in the 1520s, which led to civil war.
  • Epidemics across North America, such as those of 1781 to 1782 and 1837, emptied villages on the Plains and in the north. The 1837 outbreak nearly destroyed the Mandan.
  • It struck the Aboriginal people around Sydney in 1789, a year after the British came (smallpox at Sydney).

Inoculation with matter from a mild case was practised in China, India, Africa and the Ottoman lands, and reached Britain in the 1720s. In 1796 Edward Jenner showed that cowpox gave protection, the first vaccine (Jenner's vaccine). A World Health Organization campaign from 1967 hunted down every case. The last natural case was in Somalia in 1977, and in 1980 the world was declared free of it.
